generator.note: Four posts and ONE roof slab: 5 parts against the large-class ceiling of 8. Hand-placed, because the derivation gets two things wrong on a four-post bay. It builds only THREE posts -- the fourth corner is covered in PLAN by a box above it, so coverage reads 1.00 while a player walks straight through that post; coverage cannot see a missing part when something else shares its column. And boxes cut to the exact timber section measure WORSE than the timber, because truth cells straddle the member faces on the 0.0313 m voxel grid and their centres then fall outside every box; each post is therefore padded 0.03 m outward and 0.10 m inward. The ROOF SLAB is the change this rebuild forced, and it is a correction rather than a convenience. The deck used to be an InstancedMesh of 36 culms, which the derivation filtered as decoration, so the compound was four posts and four perimeter beams and the roof was simply absent from it. The rebuild merges the 48 culms into one mesh, nothing is filtered, and the same compound measured coverage 0.18: four fifths of the footprint is DECK, and there was no collider over any of it. A bamboo deck on purlins is a real surface -- a 9 mm gap between 70 mm culms is not something a character passes through -- so it gets one slab spanning the cell from the beam soffit at 2.340 to the cap rail at 2.600. It replaces the four beam boxes, which it contains. The bay still does NOT get a solid block under its roof: between 0.000 and 2.340 there are four posts and nothing else, which is the whole point of a prop a player walks under.
